features.title: DDL tables primary keys foreign keys and CHECK constraints
features.purpose: Define the 17 operational relations and reject invalid IDs, references, coordinates, counts and costs.

refs.needle: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT uq_users_email
refs.label: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT uq_users_email

features.demo: Open the table DDL and its named constraints. Show the failing-key/FK/CHECK test in tests/integration.test.ts. SQL enforces these rules even if the UI is bypassed.
features.say: DDL defines structure. Primary keys identify rows; foreign keys require referenced rows; CHECK and uniqueness rules reject inconsistent values.

features.title: Composite keys and multivalued attribute mapping
features.purpose: Store responder skills and resource tags as separate rows and prevent duplicate values per owner.

refs.needle: Duplicate missing invalid and unknown resource tags fail explicitly
refs.label: Duplicate missing invalid and unknown resource tags fail explicitly

features.demo: Show PRIMARY KEY(responder_id,skill) and PRIMARY KEY(resource_id,tag). Try adding an existing tag through Resources; the database rejects the duplicate.
features.say: A composite key is the combination of its columns. The same tag can belong to different resources, but it cannot be duplicated for one resource.

features.title: CREATE ALTER and DROP lifecycle
features.purpose: Demonstrate changing and removing structure without dropping operational tables.

refs.needle: CREATE ALTER and DROP operate only
refs.label: CREATE ALTER and DROP operate only

features.demo: Open database/06_ddl_demo.sql and run pnpm test. The temporary object receives a column, returns its example row and is dropped. This script is a classroom/test demonstration, not an app startup migration.
features.say: CREATE makes an object, ALTER changes its definition, and DROP removes the object itself.

features.title: Seed INSERT commands
features.purpose: Populate the relational model with 63 fictional domain records in parent-before-child order.
features.demo: Show the seed SQL and startup loader. The seed is applied only when the roles table is absent; it is not reinserted for every request. Demo password placeholders are replaced with real hashes during setup.
features.say: INSERT adds rows. Seed data makes the database and its relationships demonstrable without using real emergency data.

features.title: SQL CRUD used by the Resources screen
features.purpose: Add, list, rename and remove resource tags in PostgreSQL through the interface.
features.demo: Sign in as coordinator or technician. In Resources add a temporary tag, rename it, then remove it. Refresh and confirm persistence. A responder has no write controls and direct API/SQL writes are denied.
features.say: The form reaches the API and service, which execute bound INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE statements on resource_tags.

features.title: JOIN queries
features.purpose: Combine incidents with type/location and assignments with resource/responder information.
features.demo: Use SQL lab > Multiple JOINs for a live result. Then show dashboard() and the assignment view: JOINs also supply the operational interface.
features.say: A JOIN combines related rows by matching their keys; it does not store a second copy of each related entity.

features.title: GROUP BY HAVING COUNT and ORDER BY
features.purpose: Summarize assignments per incident and retain groups having at least one assignment.
features.demo: Choose SQL lab > GROUP BY and HAVING. Open the aggregate query to show grouping and filtering after aggregation. ORDER BY is also visible in JOIN/history queries.
features.say: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters grouped results; COUNT computes the size of a group.

features.title: Nested scalar subquery
features.purpose: Find incidents whose affected-person count exceeds the current overall average.
features.demo: Choose SQL lab > Nested query. On the untouched seed, 20 and 12 exceed 34/3, so incidents 101 and 103 qualify. Additional app-created data changes that average.
features.say: The inner AVG query returns one value; the outer query compares each incident against it.

features.title: Correlated NOT EXISTS query
features.usage: Live SQL lab example + dispatch validation
features.purpose: Find incidents without active assignments; correlated capability checks also validate a dispatch.
features.demo: Choose SQL lab > Correlated NOT EXISTS. Point to a.emergency_id=e.emergency_id. Separately show the nested capability check inside dispatch_response.
features.say: A correlated subquery refers to the current outer row. NOT EXISTS keeps it when no matching inner row exists.

features.title: CTE with ROW_NUMBER window function
features.purpose: Return the latest recorded status event for each incident.
features.demo: Choose SQL lab > CTE and window function. Explain PARTITION BY emergency_id, descending changed_at/history_id, and rn=1. This CTE is a query-explorer example; dashboard() reads history separately.
features.say: WITH names an intermediate result. ROW_NUMBER ranks each incident’s history, and rn=1 selects the newest event.

features.title: Recursive CTE
features.purpose: Generate a seven-day reporting calendar and retain dates with zero incidents.
features.demo: Choose SQL lab > Recursive CTE. The result has seven dates from 30 October to 5 November 2026. Show the anchor date, UNION ALL step, stopping condition and LEFT JOIN.
features.say: The recursive term repeatedly derives the next day until the termination condition is reached. This is a fixed demonstration interval, not a live seven-day dashboard filter.

features.title: SQL view v_assignment_summary
features.purpose: Provide reusable joined assignment/resource/responder data for the dashboard.

refs.needle: "SELECT * FROM v_assignment_summary ORDER BY assignment_id DESC"
refs.label: "SELECT * FROM v_assignment_summary ORDER BY assignment_id DESC"

features.demo: Open the CREATE VIEW definition, then dashboard() to show its real consumer. SQL lab > Assignment summary view displays the same view directly.
features.say: A normal view stores a query definition, not a separately materialized result. Our dashboard reads it as a relation.

features.title: Supporting SQL indexes
features.purpose: Support incident/status, per-incident history and assignment lookup patterns.
features.demo: Show the three CREATE INDEX statements and the generated dictionary. Explain indexed columns/order. The optimizer chooses a plan; small seed data may still use a sequential scan. No speed-up benchmark is claimed.
features.say: Indexes can help suitable lookups and sorting, but consume storage and add write maintenance.

features.title: Partial unique indexes
features.purpose: Prevent the same resource or responder from having two active/dispatched assignments while retaining historical completed assignments.

refs.needle: Conflicting dispatch is rejected with no partial assignment
refs.label: Conflicting dispatch is rejected with no partial assignment

features.demo: Show the WHERE status IN (active,dispatched) predicates. The conflicting-dispatch test demonstrates rejection; the index also independently enforces uniqueness for direct SQL writes.
features.say: Uniqueness applies only to rows matching the partial-index predicate, so past completed responses do not block future allocation.

features.title: Stored SQL function dispatch_response
features.purpose: Validate and reserve an incident response atomically, including capability coverage.
features.demo: As coordinator create a Medical incident requiring Medical support; dispatch Demo Ambulance and EMP-M01 if available. Show the SELECT dispatch_response call and resulting assignment/resource/responder/history changes.
features.say: This PostgreSQL function locks and validates the selected records, creates the assignment and updates related states together. It is invoked using SELECT, not CALL.

features.title: Stored SQL function finish_response
features.purpose: Create an assignment-linked report, release the resource/responder, and resolve the incident when no active response remains.
features.demo: Sign in as the assigned responder (medic for EMP-M01) or coordinator, select the incident and complete the response. Show ownership validation, report INSERT and release UPDATEs. Another responder is rejected.
features.say: The stored function validates ownership and commits related completion changes as one transaction.

features.title: Automatic incident-history trigger
features.purpose: Write status history automatically when an incident is created or its status actually changes.

refs.needle: Creating an incident generates exactly one audit event
refs.label: Creating an incident generates exactly one audit event

refs.needle: Unchanged status does not generate duplicate audit records
refs.label: Unchanged status does not generate duplicate audit records

features.demo: Create an incident, then dispatch and complete it. The timeline gains reported/responding/resolved entries. Show the trigger definition and its NEW/OLD status comparison. TypeScript does not call the trigger function explicitly.
features.say: The database fires the AFTER INSERT/UPDATE trigger automatically. Its history row belongs to the same transaction and disappears if that transaction rolls back.

features.title: Transactions COMMIT and ROLLBACK
features.purpose: Keep incident/requirements, dispatch reservations, reports/releases and their audit entries consistent.

refs.needle: Failed requirement insert rolls back incident and audit together
refs.label: Failed requirement insert rolls back incident and audit together

features.demo: Show asActor() wrapping the service callback in db.transaction(). Show the invalid-capability test: both incident and trigger audit row roll back. The tag demo ends with explicit ROLLBACK. The transaction wrapper commits successful callbacks and rolls back thrown errors.
features.say: A transaction groups related SQL changes so a failure leaves no partial operation. It does not make MongoDB and SQL one distributed transaction.

features.title: Row locks with FOR UPDATE
features.purpose: Lock the rows examined by dispatch/completion during their transaction.
features.demo: Open the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE statements in both stored functions. Explain their relationship to the surrounding transaction and unique active-allocation indexes. This local deployment uses one PGlite app process; it is not a multi-server load test.
features.say: FOR UPDATE holds row locks until transaction end, helping keep availability checks and state changes consistent.

features.title: Database roles GRANT REVOKE and function permissions
features.purpose: Restrict SQL actions separately from the front-end controls and service role checks.
features.demo: Show the three NOLOGIN roles and their grants. Then show asActor() selecting only a server-defined role after authentication. The integration/tag tests directly attempt forbidden SQL writes, independently of the UI.
features.say: These are group roles chosen by a trusted backend transaction, not individual database login accounts. Restricted function execution and table grants enforce database permissions.

features.title: Row level security policy
features.purpose: Reject a maintenance insert attributed to someone other than the current authenticated actor.

refs.needle: ALTER TABLE maintenance_records ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
refs.label: ALTER TABLE maintenance_records ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY

refs.needle: Database role grants and RLS enforce maintenance author identity
refs.label: Database role grants and RLS enforce maintenance author identity

features.demo: Show WITH CHECK(performed_by=app_actor()). The test inserts as a technician with another author ID and expects failure. The API also supplies the author from the session.
features.say: GRANT controls which operations a role may attempt; RLS adds a row-level condition to those operations.

features.title: Bound SQL parameters and query allowlist
features.purpose: Keep submitted values separate from SQL syntax and restrict the query explorer to predefined SQL.
features.demo: Show a $1/$2 parameterized query and its values array, then the labQueries key check. There is no endpoint that executes arbitrary user-entered SQL.
features.say: The service passes values separately from the SQL statement. An allowlist chooses the statement itself.

features.title: Authentication password hashes and session storage
features.purpose: Authenticate role accounts without persisting a plaintext password or raw session token.
features.demo: Show scrypt plus random salts, SHA-256 token hashing, the session expiry query and HttpOnly/SameSite cookie. Secure setup uses hidden terminal input. These TypeScript helpers are application functions, not stored SQL routines.
features.say: Passwords are verified against salted hashes; the browser has a random cookie token while SQL stores only its hash.

features.title: MongoDB database and collection creation
features.purpose: Use a real document database for variable incident field updates.
features.demo: Open mongo() to show the real MongoClient connection and collection creation. The application initializes the collection on first note access; the mongosh file is a separate fresh-database demonstration.
features.say: MongoDB holds incident-linked field-note documents; PostgreSQL holds structured operational relationships.

features.title: MongoDB collection validation
features.purpose: Require valid incident/author IDs, bounded note text, tags, assessment objects and date fields even for direct document inserts.

refs.needle: MongoDB collection validator rejects malformed direct inserts
refs.label: MongoDB collection validator rejects malformed direct inserts

features.demo: Show $jsonSchema required/properties and validationAction:error. The integration test writes an incomplete document directly and confirms MongoDB rejects it, independently of Zod.
features.say: API validation checks requests, while collection validation protects the stored document shape at the database level.

features.title: MongoDB compound and text indexes
features.purpose: Support per-incident chronological retrieval and keyword search across note text and tags.
features.demo: Show both createIndex calls and their matching find/sort/$text queries. Explain column order and the separate text index. Do not claim a measured speed-up from the small demo dataset.
features.say: The compound index organizes incident/time access; the text index enables $text keyword retrieval.

features.title: MongoDB CREATE insertOne
features.purpose: Save a field note with server-derived author and creation/update timestamps.
features.demo: In Field notes select an incident and save a text update with two tags and an optional assessment. The API returns the inserted ObjectId and the saved note appears after refresh.
features.say: insertOne creates a document. The server obtains author_id from the authenticated session rather than trusting an author supplied by the browser.

features.title: MongoDB READ find sort and limit
features.purpose: Read up to 100 notes for the selected SQL incident in newest-first order.
features.demo: Select another incident in Field notes. Show the emergency_id filter, created_at sort and limit(100). Results are incident-specific, not a dump of the whole collection.
features.say: find selects matching documents, sort orders them and limit bounds the response.

features.title: MongoDB UPDATE updateOne and $set
features.purpose: Edit note text/tags/assessment while retaining its author, creation date and incident link.
features.demo: Use Edit note as its author or coordinator, save changes and refresh. Show ownedNote() and the editable-field schema before updateOne. The incident ID is not an editable field.
features.say: $set changes selected fields instead of replacing the entire document. Ownership is checked before the update.

features.title: MongoDB DELETE deleteOne
features.purpose: Delete only an authorized field note selected by ObjectId.
features.demo: Create a disposable note and delete it using Delete note. Confirm it disappears after reload. A different responder cannot delete a note they do not own.
features.say: deleteOne removes the matching document after the shared ownership/reference checks.

features.title: Full text search with $text
features.purpose: Search selected-incident note text and tags using MongoDB’s text index.
features.demo: Save a note containing a distinctive word such as evacuation, then search it in Field notes. Show the incident filter plus $text query and the text-index definition.
features.say: This is indexed keyword search, not vector similarity or semantic embeddings.

features.title: MongoDB aggregation pipeline
features.purpose: Count field-note tag occurrences for the selected incident.
features.demo: Add a note tagged medical and safety. Each tag’s count increases by one. Show $match, $unwind, $group, $sort and $limit, then the tag-summary display.
features.say: The pipeline selects one incident, turns each array tag into a row-like item and groups those items to count occurrences.

features.title: Cross database references and note ownership
features.purpose: Validate SQL incident existence/assignment scope before MongoDB writes and enforce author/coordinator edit rights.

refs.needle: NoSQL validates SQL references assignment scope and ownership
refs.label: NoSQL validates SQL references assignment scope and ownership

features.demo: Show ensureIncident() and ownedNote(). Tests reject an unknown SQL incident, an unassigned responder and another author’s edit. SQL foreign keys do not reach into MongoDB.
features.say: The API maintains these cross-database references. There is no distributed foreign key or shared SQL/MongoDB transaction.

features.title: Database outage failure handling
features.purpose: Return an explicit failed/unconfirmed note operation while keeping independent SQL functionality available.

refs.needle: "MongoDB is unavailable. The note was not saved;
refs.label: "MongoDB is unavailable. The note was not saved;

features.demo: Open the isolated offline test and docs/verification/offline.json. It starts a separate app with an unavailable MongoDB URI and expects HTTP 503 for a note write and HTTP 200 for the SQL dashboard. No need to stop the live demo database.
features.say: A MongoDB failure is shown as a failure, not a successful save. SQL and MongoDB remain independent services.

features.title: Learned sentence embeddings
features.purpose: Encode incident descriptions and questions as normalized 384-dimensional vectors using the same pinned local MiniLM model.
features.demo: Run pnpm vector:setup once. In Incidents search A warehouse is burning. Show the model identity and 384 dimensions in the API result. We use real model inference, not manual vectors or keyword substitutions.
features.say: The model turns sentences into numeric representations. Identical model and preprocessing are required for document and query vectors.

features.title: pgvector cosine distance and HNSW index
features.purpose: Retrieve semantically related past incidents using a database-native nearest-neighbour query.

refs.needle: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector
refs.label: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector

features.demo: Search People trapped by rising water and inspect ranked incidents. Show embedding <=> query, ORDER BY distance and LIMIT. Smaller distance is closer; the score is not probability. Small tables may use a sequential scan.
features.say: This implements the course PostgreSQL vector lesson within our existing architecture. MongoDB notes still use keyword search.

features.title: Embedding invalidation and incremental indexing
features.purpose: Prevent a description edit from leaving a searchable embedding for old text, while keeping incident reporting independent of the model.
features.demo: Show the BEFORE description-update trigger. It clears vectors only for changed descriptions; the next search recomputes them. Inference happens outside transactions and updates compare source text to avoid stale writes.
features.say: Embeddings are a derived search representation. Invalidating and regenerating them keeps search consistent with the source incident.
